study_identification_part.si4_title: Capturing the Individual Deviations From Normative Models of Brain Structure for Depression Diagnosis and Treatment

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the objective to investigate depression using individual deviations from normative ranges of GMV and outline three applications: classification with external validation and Bayesian analyses for treatment-related latent factors.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We investigated the clinical issues related to depression according to individual deviations from normative ranges of gray matter volume." … "Based on this, we developed three applications… 1) … We also explored the performance … in an independent external test set. 2) A Bayesian model … SSRIs … 3) … SSRIs and SNRIs."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: A new normative model was built using open healthy datasets (HCP and REST-meta-MDD), with sample sizes specified and original sources cited. They report excluding participants with poor imaging quality/incomplete data and give final sample sizes. However, explicit eligibility criteria and image quality standards for the open reference datasets and specific exclusion reasons in those datasets are not detailed.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "… downloaded phenotypic data and MRI T1-weighted data from the Human Connectome Project (dataset II; 510 HC participants …) and REST-meta-MDD Project (dataset III; 229 HC participants …)." … "Participants with incomplete clinical data or poor imaging quality were also excluded. Ultimately, 127 depressed patients and 110 HCs … In addition, 60 patients and 56 HCs … were used as an external test set."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled in the normative model; multi-site effects are addressed using ComBat while retaining biological variability for age, sex, and TIV.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "… predict GMV … for a given age and sex …"; "… we used the ComBat method … retained the biological variability related to age, sex, and TIV …"

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data sources of the reference cohort are clearly specified as HCP and REST-meta-MDD, including sample sizes and age ranges.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "… Human Connectome Project (dataset II; 510 HC participants; age range, 22–36 years) and REST-meta-MDD Project (dataset III; 229 HC participants; age range, 18–65 years; site 20)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data (existing datasets HCP and REST-meta-MDD) were used for the reference cohort, so acquisition protocol details are not required per guide.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: Datasets I–II processed with CAT12/SPM12 (bias correction, segmentation, DARTEL normalization to MNI, 8-mm FWHM smoothing); Dataset III processed with DPARSF/SPM and similarly smoothed.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "… preprocessed with default parameter setting in CAT12 … implemented in SPM12 … DARTEL … normalized to MNI … smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8-mm FWHM." … "Dataset III … preprocessed using DPARSF … Similarly … smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8-mm FWHM."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No data partitioning (e.g., cross-validation/hold-out) within the reference cohort (datasets II–III) is described. They assessed generality by applying the model to an independent HC set (dataset I), which is external rather than internal validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To verify the generality of normative models, the HCs in discovery cohort of Dataset I … were directly applied to obtain the deviations from the normal distribution constructed via large samples from Dataset II&III."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model was applied to an independent external dataset of HCs (dataset I) to check coverage/calibration, showing >95% within the normative range.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "… more than 95% of HCs were within the normative range for the majority of brain regions … confirming that the normative models were not predicting an excessive number of deviations (i.e., more than 95% of individuals were within the 2.5% to 97.5% confidence interval)."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify B-spline Bayesian linear regression for regionwise normative modeling and the use of PCNtoolkit. They also define the z-score threshold (|z| ≥ 1.96) for extreme deviations.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Estimate of the normative model with B-spline Bayesian linear regression for each brain region …"; "All the analyses were performed in Python 3.6, using the PCNtoolkit … for model estimation and evaluation. We established the threshold for NPM using |z| ±1.96 …"

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: They report calibration coverage (>95% within 2.5–97.5% CI in HCs) and note regional correlation between predicted and true values in training data (excluding regions with low correlation).
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: ">95% of HCs were within the normative range … (2.5% to 97.5% CI)."; "… correlations between the predicted and true value in the training data … were low (less than 0.5) in bilateral thalamus, which were not included …"

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning was performed for the reference cohort; per guide, this item is not applicable.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and library versions are provided (Python 3.6.13, SPM, CAT12, ComBat, PCNtoolkit, LIBSVM). Availability of code and trained models is not stated.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "Python v3.6.13"; "SPM MATLAB package"; "CAT12 MATLAB package"; "ComBat Python package"; "PCNtoolkit Python package"; "LIBSVM MATLAB package" (Key Resources Table).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection: DSM-IV diagnosis by at least two attending doctors; HAMD-17 used; explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria; quality control and completeness criteria; final sample sizes and sites reported.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "According to the DSM (4th Edition), all depression patients were diagnosed by at least two attending doctors and assessed by the HAMD-17 … Participants with incomplete clinical data or poor imaging quality were also excluded. Ultimately, 127 depressed patients and 110 HCs … In addition, 60 patients and 56 HCs … external test set."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses considered clinical subgrouping by treatment class (SSRIs vs SNRIs) and response status defined by HAMD-17, but there is no explicit adjustment for additional clinical covariates (e.g., illness duration, medication history) in deviation-score analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "… patients with at least a 50% reduction in the total scores of 17-item HAMD after 4 weeks were … responders …"; "The discrete z-scores within two different subdivided patient populations (SSRI: responder vs. non-responder; responder: SSRIs vs. SNRIs) were fed into the polar LDA model …"

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection sites and time period are described (NBH and NDTH; Sep 2011–Dec 2020).
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Participants were recruited … in NBH and NDTH between September 2011 and December 2020."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are reported for discovery and external test cohorts; demographic and clinical characteristics (e.g., age and HAMD-17 scores) are tabulated in the supplement.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "Ultimately, 127 depressed patients and 110 HCs … 60 patients and 56 HCs …"; "Age (year) …"; "HAMD-17 (baseline)… (after 4 weeks)…"

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures and procedures are specified: DSM-IV diagnosis and HAMD-17 severity assessment; treatment response defined by ≥50% HAMD-17 reduction at 4 weeks.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "According to the DSM (4th Edition) … assessed by the HAMD-17 for depression severity … patients with at least a 50% reduction … after four weeks were … responders."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are defined as z-scores from the normative model, with thresholds |z| ≥ 1.96 for extreme deviations. Clinical implications are discussed, including improved diagnostic classification and treatment-related latent factors.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "We established the threshold for NPM using |z| ±1.96 … to define the extreme positive or negative deviations …"; "… our normative modeling approach revealed highly individualized patterns … models trained with individual normative probability maps … verified in an independent external test set. Furthermore, different latent brain structural factors in relation to antidepressant treatment were revealed by a Bayesian model …"
